recipes.name: Airport Bob's Green Beans
ingredients_raw: 6 thick slices bacon, cut into 1 inch pieces
1 (16 ounce) package frozen cut green beans

steps.text: Fry the bacon in a large skillet over medium heat until done, but not quite crisp, about 9 minutes. Drain off grease and add butter and brown sugar. Cook and stir over medium heat until sugar has dissolved; remove from the heat and set aside.

Place the green beans into a pot and fill with about 1 inch of water. Bring to a boil then cover, and steam over medium heat until cooked through, about 5 minutes. Drain off water and stir in the sugar and bacon mixture. Serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Airport Bob's Green Beans
raw_recipe.description: A simple, sweet, green bean and bacon side that others will crave.

review.reviewBody: The last laugh is on me....I just fixed these on a whim because I had everything on hand and trying to use up part of a bag of frozen green beans. Actually, I thought the recipe sounded rather "icky" but was I ever WRONG ! These are the BEST !! Usually I go for lemony flavors on veggies, etc., but Airport Bob's Green Beans are OUT OF THIS WORLD ! I used peppered bacon. I've already shared the recipe with two other foodies. SCRUMPTIOUS !

This was the first time that I have ever been able to get my children to eat all of the green beans on their plate. I got bacon slices straight from the butcher and then, as suggested from other reviewers, I used fresh green beans and steamed them in my steamer pot first. Everything else I kept the same. Yum!

This is great. Some times I also sauté some fresh mushrooms and some chopped onions in the bacon grease and then Drain it all and then mix the bacon, onions and mushrooms with the beans and butter and brown sugar mixture. If I am taking it to a party I put it in the crockpot.

Like other reviewers suggested, I steamed the green beans instead of boiling them, and I sauteed some garlic. I also veganized this recipe by using butter from Earth Balance Soy Garden and Organic Matter Vegan Bacon. This "bacon" is made from coconut flakes and comes already crispy in the bag, so no cooking and no fat draining required. I got the nice bacon flavor in addition to a hint of coconut, which was a great touch!

These were amazing. I cut the brown sugar back to about an 1/8th of a cup, used fresh green beans and steamed them. There was the touch of sweetness with the crispy bacon. The entire dish was gone by the end of the meal. No leftovers for lunch!

This is an awesome recipe ~ but warning...Don't overcook the butter/brown sugar mixture b/c it will thicken to a consistency which is not usable. I had to throw out my first batch b/c this mixture had hardened. I'm so glad that I retried it though b/c it came out perfect & so tasty. I cut the recipe in half due to the amount of people I was serving & per other reviews, I steamed my green beans (which came out perfect) & added garlic and red pepper flakes. This will be the only way I serve green beans in the future ~ So Yummy!

This was a hit on Thanksgiving. The only thing I have to change is the directions for the bacon. Everyone wished the bacon was crispy but the directions said not to cook til crispy. I thought it would crisp up in the butter/sugar mixture but it didn't. So next time, I'll top the beans with crispy bacon before serving. I also didn't use thick cut bacon but I will next time. I think it would be better with thicker bacon.
I added garlic and red pepper and sautéed the green beans in the sauce for about 10 minutes while the rest of dinner finished. SO good!!!

I liked the sweet buttery taste, especially during the winter months. I added half a sweet onion, diced, and 1/2 t of dried sage, which I thought gave a bit of savory to complement the sweet. Many compliments from our church group (humbly speaking).
I made these per the recipe with the exception that I used some of the bacon drippings instead of the butter. My family really liked these.

Everything is better with bacon, right? The first time I made these I followed the recipe exactly and it was just too much butter. Because of the bacon flavor it is not necessary to add 1/4 c of butter. I know only use about 1 or 2 tbsp butter or just enough to melt the brown sugar. I tend to use less sugar too, but not less bacon!! =)
Added some cayenne pepper ,just a touch

I was trying to find a new way to prepare the abundance of green beans that we are getting from our garden at this time of year and discovered this recipe. My expectations were high after reading the reviews, but I don't think I will make this again. I didn't care for the sweetness and would rather just go with bacon and maybe some onions.
Always a hit! Thanks

I followed the directions exactly and was extremely disappointed. Maybe I cooked the beans for to long but I did the 5 minutes like the instructions said to and it turned out mushy and not very flavorful. We did not eat it.
My kids ask for it every thanksgiving!
this recipe is amazing! my husband requests them atleast once a week

I agree with another review. Sugar and green beans do not go together. My sauce also got hard but I heated it back up. I'm giving three stars instead of two because they went well with my barbecue meatloaf.
Everyone loved it. Even my 13 year old son who doesn’t like vegetables. Followed directions exactly and it turned out great.
Tasty !
